scope: D7 Layout occurrence duplication owner intent, D6 empty-Show verification, and the complete prepared v2 command catalogue with its census, size oracle, coverage maps, versioned resources and #1029 MCP sequence
invariants: D7: duplication inserts one fresh occurrence of the same definition, duration and parameters immediately after the source; Show End grows by exactly that duration.
D7: every authored entity at or after the source end moves later exactly once; content inside the interval keeps its authored times.
D7: duplication mints no Pattern runtime; copies retain instanceId, entryPolicy, sampling and Group runtime bindings.
D7: identity is never allocated inside the owner; an inexact, colliding, blank or duplicated identity plan refuses before any change.
D7: content crossing the duplicated boundary refuses; the owner never extends, splits, holds or reroutes it.
D6: final Clip deletion leaves a structurally valid, editable and saveable empty Show; no v1 last-Clip refusal remains on the v2 path.
Rule 1: every command addresses entities by stable identity; no scene_id, index, overlay index, Boundary time lookup or target_clip_id survives.
Rule 2: every _ms field is a bounded safe-integer millisecond; intervals are half-open.
Rule 3: every name uses the closed verb vocabulary; delete_ and reset_ retire.
Rule 4: an already-satisfied valid request returns unchanged with zero changes for every command, creates no history, timestamp or save, and never aborts its batch.
Rule 5: no json field kind; closed sets are enums, described ranges carry schema bounds, null appears only where clearing is documented, bulk arrays are 1-128.
Rule 6: a changed command reports the same fourteen affected collections, translated from the owner result without invention, widening or loss.
Rule 7: a v1 refusal code is reused only where its meaning is unchanged; the owner's typed code passes through unaltered.
Rule 8: tools/list through the in-process probe stays inside the size budget.
Rule 9: read_show returns the record version the bound editor holds; the v1 double representation ends at cutover.
Rule 10: a singular command is the bulk schema fragment of one; every retired singular setter stays unregistered.
A command never restates a domain rule: it resolves identities, mints the fresh identities a pure owner requires, and adopts the owner result.
Refusal and no-op return the preimage record by reference with no changes.
The catalogue is prepared, not activated: production MCP keeps v1 until #1039.

D3 instance policy: sole with one match / sole with several / new with none / new with an existing / explicit instance id / unknown instance id
appearance apply: whole-clip / at-time on an existing key / at-time inserting a fresh key with later keys retained
replace: shared runtime forked versus sole runtime retained; resolver present / absent / source unresolvable
descriptor shape: empty bulk array / over 128 items / negative time / unknown field / missing exactly-one / both exactly-one / retired enum member
addressing: unknown Clip, Transition, Layout interval, Marker, Property track, Layer, Zone Layout and Group occurrence, with and without existing candidates
no-op matrix: one already-satisfied request per command, alone and inside a batch that still applies its other change

redEvidence: 6/6 duplication cases failed before the owner intent existed: an unknown intent fell through to the shared occurrence branch, and the empty/final-occurrence cases reported the unshifted preimage.

The catalogue's first full run failed 9/24 behavioural cases, each for a real reason: a stored Transition needs structured easing rather than a preset string; insertion past Show End is an invalid result; a plain resize belongs to the temporal owner, not the Transition owner's connected resize; reassigning a Layer into an occupied Layer is a materialized collision refusal.
The size oracle failed at 71,043 bytes against the 65,536 budget before the Aperture shape-parameter record and the description trim.
faults: Dropping the Transition endpoint-straddle guard in the duplicate owner: 'refuses when authored content crosses the duplicated occurrence boundary' failed (1/6), restored green.
Shifting later Clip starts without their appearance keys: two duplication cases failed (2/6), restored green.
Turning the uniform no-op into a refusal: the no-op matrix plus the independence and Layout-uniqueness no-ops failed (3/44), restored green.

Emptying the candidate list on an unknown identity: the addressing case failed (1/44) after the assertion was strengthened from 'defined' to 'contains the identity that exists'; the first, weaker assertion did not kill it.

Replacing the owner's typed refusal code with engine-refused: five cases failed (5/44) across Show End protection, Layer reassignment, Layout interval removal, boundary-crossing duplication and owner parity, restored green.

The cause is the resize_clip activity summary rewording that landed in 'Refine Show agent activity for #1018' (30a0aa00, 2026-09-12), four days after the fixture evidence was pinned by '#950 Stabilize baseline fixture resize evidence' (c0ab5995, 2026-09-08). The base commit d46eeae1 already shows this difference and this slice changes nothing on the v1 harness path, so the pinned evidence is left untouched rather than re-recorded.
residualGaps: Moving a Clip to another Zone or Layer has no landed v2 owner intent: showClipTemporalV2 owns only the time edges and editShowTransitionV2 refuses a connected component that changes Zone or Layer. update_clips refuses it with a typed unsupported code naming the missing capability. Smallest counterexample: v1 accepts move_clip { clip_id, layer: 1 }; v2 has no owner intent that writes clip.layerId outside editShowLayerV2's complete removal reassignment.

Marker role: chapter is specification section 3 delta 7 and lands with #1040. add_marker and update_marker accept the argument and refuse it with a typed unsupported code rather than dropping it silently.
Duplicating a Layout interval with content refuses a copied Transition that carries propertyRamps (unsupported-content-copy); the caller projects those ramps into tracks first.

The #1029 transcript is proven at the real MCP tool boundary and over the real v2 catalogue and importers, not through a live browser editor: agentPrivateExecutor and editorAdmission still apply v1 commands to a v1 capture, and binding them to the v2 pilot record is #1039's coordinated activation, whose deployed transcript is that issue's named gate.

The harness grammar, corpus and baseline fixtures are proven complete against the name map but are not themselves rewritten onto v2; they drive the v1 editor route and move with the same #1039 activation.

CONTEXT.md is unchanged: every concept a v2 command name surfaces (Clip, Layer, Zone Layout interval, Transition, Marker, Pattern instance, Group occurrence, Show End, Restart) is already defined there.
